version_source: the service's push response: 'Kernel version 2 successfully pushed'
dataset: marsmanam/persian-voice-eval, the version staged from 007af09, verified by download before the push
hypothesis: Version 1 showed the official SDPA configuration runs out of memory on a T4 in its first forward pass at 8,192 tokens per GPU. The official recipe fits a T4 pair unchanged in its arithmetic if the LLM's activations are recomputed in the backward pass (gradient checkpointing) and DDP's gradient buckets share the gradients' storage - and, failing that, with AdamW applying the same update one tensor at a time. The test: the SDPA configuration with those techniques runs 8 optimizer steps on both GPUs; and on one GPU at a test-only 512-token batch, the first loss and the gradients before the first update match the official path's.
environment: as v1: every pinned package matched (torch 2.8.0+cu128, torchaudio 2.8.0+cu128, transformers 5.3.0, accelerate 1.13.0, webdataset 1.0.2, safetensors 0.7.0, tokenizers 0.22.2, huggingface-hub 1.7.2); numpy 2.0.2 against the lock's 2.4.3, not pinned; omnivoice 0.2.1 from git at 08be0b4c; evidence/omnivoice-probe-v2/environment.json

measured.unchanged: the checkpointed path computed the same loss and the same gradients as the official path in the test above. DDP bucket views exist only with two processes, so the one-GPU test does not cover them; they are an aliasing of the gradient buffers that DDP documents as not changing the reduction

budget.sessions: at least 3 of up to 12 hours, because a checkpoint every 500 steps (1.94 h) is where a session can stop
budget.basis: 5,000 x 13.98 s; tokenising 127.85 h at 36x real time; ten official evaluations of the 3.68 h valid split at the slice's rate. Checkpoint saves and start-up are extra

not_tested: whether step time holds over the whole training split (batch shapes vary with clip length); whether the memory peak stays under the card on the longest batches; the tokeniser's rate at full scale
